Damian Paletta
 
Are Democrats About to Make a Big Move in the South?
 
Plus, Sen. Susan Collins faces the fight of her long political life, and are you a conservative or a liberal?
 
 
LEKAN OYEKANMI/AP
 

Good morning. President Trump is making repeated trips to Texas in an effort to prevent Democrat James Talarico from winning a long-held GOP Senate seat.

 

On Monday, the president was in Mississippi, trying to help Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith fend off a Democratic challenger. And Trump is headed back to South Carolina on Thursday to try to help GOP Sen. Darline Graham.

 

In the Georgia governor’s race, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms is neck-and-neck with Republican candidate Rick Jackson (and Democrat Sen. Jon Ossoff is up big in many polls there).

 

What. On. Earth. Is. Going. On?

 

In 2016, Trump blasted through what is known as the “Blue Wall,” winning Democratic strongholds of Pennsylvania, Michigan and Wisconsin.

 

It was those states that appeared to be the biggest modern tug of war in American politics, but Democrats’ stealthy advance into the South during this midterm cycle could end up being the story of the year. (Democrats are trying to crack through some walls in the Midwest, too).

 

Democrats have quite a history in the South, but it has mostly been history. They lost a tremendous amount of ground there in the past decade. Sure, Joe Biden won Georgia in 2020. Was that a blip, or the beginning of something?

 

Of course, Jimmy Carter was from Plains, Ga. Lyndon Baines Johnson was a Texan. And Bill Clinton is from Arkansas. Are Democrats drawing up a new map?

 

We will know a lot more in a week.

 

This is an edition of the Politics newsletter, bringing you an expert guide to what’s driving D.C. every day. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

People and Policies I’m Watching

 

Interest rate: The Federal Reserve will announce its latest decision at 2 p.m. ET.

 

Melania Trump: A ceasefire brokered by the first lady took effect in a starving Ukrainian city.

 

Israel election: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party moved into the lead position, though it is still sitting short of a majority.

 

Trump’s Wednesday: The president will hold a series of policy meetings before an evening midterm rally in Ohio.

 
 
 

What I’m Following

 
 
DANIEL ALEXANDER ORR FOR WSJ
 

Susan Collins is in the fight of her political life. The Maine senator faces the most difficult re-election campaign of her long career. She is trying to fend off intense political headwinds, along with a bombshell report involving donations to a pro-Collins super PAC by a politically connected federal contractor.

 

Are you a conservative or a liberal? As the midterms approach, it seems the country is split, but conservatives and liberals agree on some of the top policy ideas. Take our quiz to find out how your view of these ideas compares with those of people in our latest survey.

 

Trump and Talarico rallied voters in Texas just miles apart. Both were making their final push in the Lone Star state to win voter support just one week out from the midterm elections. Talarico has consistently maintained a narrow lead in the polls, but the race is on track to become the most expensive Senate contest in history.

 
 
 

What Else Is Happening

 

• The U.S. told several Gulf Arab nations to prepare for a possible short military campaign against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections.

 

• The Trump administration plans to issue visas to Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family.

 

• The Trump administration is moving to dismantle Biden-era rules that sought to limit methane emissions from the oil-and-gas industry.
